transcript.content: Hi, welcome in—I'm Dr. [Name]. What brings you in to see me today?

Hi. I'm here because... I just don't care about anything anymore. 

I just sit in my room while everything kind of slips away. I used to do things, but now I don't care about my art classes, or board-game nights. I don't even have any interest in hiking or getting back to my soccer team. I just... I don't care about any of it.
How long have you been feeling this way—not caring about the things you used to enjoy?
It became pretty constant around last summer. So... I guess it's been about a year and four months now that I've just felt like this.
Have you ever had a period—lasting several days or more—where you felt unusually energetic, elated, or needed much less sleep than usual, even if it happened before this current stretch of low mood?
No, I haven't. I've just felt... like this. Tired and empty. I don't remember ever feeling super energetic or anything like that.

Before this started about 16 months ago, had you ever gone through a separate period—weeks or months at some earlier point in your life—where you felt similarly depressed or lost interest in things, followed by a stretch where you felt back to your normal self?

No, I don't think so. I mean, I've had normal bad days or weeks like anyone else, but nothing like this. This is the first time it's been this bad and just... stayed this way. Before last summer, I was pretty much myself.
Over this past 16 months, have you noticed any changes in your sleep—such as trouble falling asleep, staying asleep, or sleeping much more than usual?

Yeah, my sleep is... it's pretty bad. I lie awake for hours at night. I just end up checking the door over and over, and listening to see if I hear anything. Then when I do finally fall asleep, I wake up way before dawn. I'll just be shaking, and I can't get back to sleep after that.
Around the time this started 16 months ago, did something frightening, dangerous, or traumatic happen to you?
No, nothing like that happened. I mean, there wasn't any big accident or... or anything dangerous that started all this. It just sort of began on its own, I guess.
Do you find yourself worrying excessively about a lot of different things—like your health, safety, or everyday responsibilities—and having a hard time controlling or stopping that worry?

No, not really. I mean, I get scared at night, like I was saying before... but I don't really worry about normal things. Like my health, or everyday chores, or anything like that. I honestly don't have the energy to care about those kinds of responsibilities right now anyway. So, no, it's not really that kind of worry.
When you're lying awake checking the door and listening for sounds, what exactly are you afraid might happen?

I know it sounds impossible, but... I'm just sure the people downstairs, and maybe some of my ex's friends, are watching me. I think they've been tracking when I leave the apartment. Because... well, the hallway lights blink right after I even just think about going to the store. So I stay awake, just listening, to make sure they aren't coming up here.
Do these feelings of being watched or tracked happen only during this stretch when you've been feeling depressed, or have you noticed them at other times as well, even if your mood improved?

No, it's not just when I'm this depressed. There was a stretch, um, before the worst of the depression really set in... where my mood was actually okay. I could still cook sometimes, and I was still answering my friends when they reached out. But even during that time, for weeks, I was already hearing the voice, and I already believed the hallway lights were signals about me. So, yeah, it was definitely happening before the depression got this bad.
During that earlier stretch when your mood was okay, how many weeks did you continue hearing the voice and believing you were being watched before the depression set in?

Um, I guess it was about... maybe three or four weeks? Like I said, I was doing okay then. I was making dinner, texting people back. But the whole time, for that whole month or so, I was hearing that voice and seeing the lights blink when I walked by. It was happening the whole time, even before I started feeling so down.
Are you still hearing that voice and still feeling like you're being watched right now, during this depressed period, or has that gone away?

Yeah, it hasn't gone away. I'm definitely still hearing it right now. Actually... for much of this past year, the low mood and the voices have been happening at the exact same time. I'll just be lying in bed, feeling totally hopeless, and while I'm feeling like that, I'm also hearing that woman telling me I ruined everything. So, yes, they're definitely both happening right now.
I'm not really sure what else to say about all that. Did you have another question?
Over this past year, have you also noticed changes in your appetite or weight, or found yourself feeling unusually guilty, worthless, or having trouble concentrating?

Yeah, my appetite has definitely changed. I go most of the day without eating now. It's just... food tastes like cardboard to me, so I don't really see the point. And I've definitely lost weight. My jeans have gotten so loose lately that I actually have to knot the waistband just to keep them up. As for the other stuff, I mean, I do feel guilty and worthless a lot, like I mentioned before, just lying in bed feeling hopeless. And concentrating is really hard, especially with the voice constantly talking at me.

inference.note: Confirmed full depressive syndrome (anhedonia, weight/appetite loss, guilt, poor concentration, sleep disturbance) occurring concurrently with persistent psychotic symptoms (voices, delusions of being watched) for about a year, with an earlier ~4-week period of isolated psychotic symptoms before mood decline. This pattern—prominent mood episode co-occurring with psychotic symptoms, not merely psychotic disorder with secondary depression—supports schizoaffective disorder over schizophrenia alone, so F20.9 is ruled out.

final_diagnosis.reason: The patient reports a continuous illness episode of about 16 months in which mood symptoms (anhedonia, hopelessness, guilt, appetite/weight loss, poor concentration, sleep disturbance) meeting criteria for a major depressive episode co-occur with psychotic symptoms (auditory hallucination of a derogatory voice, persecutory delusions about being watched/tracked). Critically, there was a distinct 3-4 week period prior to the depressive episode worsening during which the patient's mood was largely intact (she could cook, engage socially) yet she continued to experience the auditory hallucinations and delusional beliefs, establishing that psychotic symptoms occurred for a significant period in the absence of a full mood episode. This pattern—overlapping mood and psychotic symptoms for the majority of the illness course, with psychotic symptoms also present for at least 2 weeks without prominent mood symptoms—fits Schizoaffective Disorder, Depressive Type (F25.1) rather than Major Depressive Disorder with psychotic features (F32.3, which requires psychosis only during mood episodes) or Schizophrenia (F20.9, which would require absence of a prominent mood syndrome accounting for most of the illness). No manic/hypomanic episodes, trauma-based PTSD symptoms, or GAD-type worry were identified, and no prior mood episodes before this index episode were reported.
